podcast.title: Death (September 16, 1977)
podcast.body: Mark Bowen died on September 16, 1977, when his girlfriend, Gloria Jones, crashed their Mini Cooper into a tree in southwest London. "Mark Bowlin died on September 16, 1977, when his girlfriend Gloria Jones drove their mini-cooper into a tree in southwest London."

podcast.title: Early Career - Taranosaurus Rex
podcast.body: Mark Bowen, a London-based singer-songwriter and poet, began his career with the psychedelic folk band Taranosaurus Rex. This band released four largely acoustic albums in the 1960s but did not achieve significant hit success. "Bowen was a London-based singer-songwriter and poet. He started with a psychedelic folk band called Taranosaurus Rex, who released four largely acoustic albums in the 1960s without managing to have a proper hit."

podcast.title: Glam Rock Appearance on Top of the Pops
podcast.body: In March 1971, after "Ride a White Swan" became a hit, Mark Bowen appeared on Top of the Pops wearing satin clothes and glitter. This striking visual, in a "grey recession-ridden still in the post-war Doldrums England," was seen as fresh and new, further enhanced by Bowen's "petite and cute and non-threatening" appearance which had a "fluid" quality about it. "But in March 1971, Bowen appeared on the show wearing satin clothes and glitter."

podcast.title: Impact on Sexual Identity
podcast.body: Mark Bowen's glittery, satiny, and somewhat sexually ambiguous public persona on TV, especially given his height of five foot four, resonated deeply in early 1970s Britain, where homosexuality had only recently been decriminalized (1967 Sexual Offences Act) but public displays remained illegal. For some, his appearance pushed boundaries, while for others, it offered a liberating affirmation of their own non-binary feelings. "Now, for some, a pretty glittery, satiny, five foot four Mark Bowen on TV was really close to that line about doing something gay in public. For others, though, it was not just a breath of fresh air. It was also like, hey, that's me. I feel like that. And it's okay to be that way."

podcast.title: Transformation to T-Rex
podcast.body: Frustrated by a lack of success or sensing a shift in the musical landscape, Bowen shortened the band's name to T-Rex and transitioned to playing an electric guitar, which marked a turning point in his career. "Bowen shortened the name to T-Rex and picked up an electric guitar."

xref.title: Hype Costumes (1970)
xref.body: In 1970, with his band Hype, Bowie began experimenting with stage costumes. They wore superhero outfits made from shiny material, thigh-high boots, and Bowie's own costume included a cape and the word "rainbow man" sewn on his chest, a stark contrast to the hippie fashion of the time. "In 1970, around the time Mark Bowen was gaining fame with Ride-A-White Swan, Bowie had a band called Hype. They began appearing in interesting costumes."
